You are the implementer for unit c1-ringer-cleanup (post-run cleanup of the "Jev in ringer" work in ringer.py), running as a ringer worker with no conversation history; everything you need is in this spec.

WORKSPACE AND BOUNDARY
- Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the ringer repo, detached at the current commit of branch jev-ringer; edit files here directly and run every command from here.
- Never read from, edit, or run commands inside /home/jjrdar/repos/ringer (the main checkout).
- Leave every change uncommitted: never run `git commit`, `git stash`, `git reset`, `git checkout`, or anything else that moves HEAD; the check stages and exports your diff.
- Never create or modify a path outside the ownership list below.
- Never set or export TYPESAFE_API_KEY and never make a network call.
- Never use the em dash character (Unicode U+2014); use a plain "-".
- Match the surrounding code style; add no comments beyond what the change needs.

OWNERSHIP LIST (the only paths you may modify)
- ringer.py
- tests/test_jev_plumbing.py
- tests/test_jev_task_type.py

CONTEXT
The FAIL flag feature was cancelled for good. Its config switch (`JevConfig.fail_flag`, `fail_flag_cutoff`), the questions `JEV_FAIL_QUESTIONS`, `decide_fail_flag`, and `scripts/jev_fail_replay.py` STAY. Only the two hooks that were created for the never-built retry-path wiring go. Three independent changes, all required:

CHANGE 1 - the check-output marker writer uses the shared constant
ringer.py defines `JEV_CHECK_OUTPUT_MARKER = "raw_check_output_first_2000_chars:\n"` (note the trailing newline) and the reader `jev_check_output_from_notes` uses it. The writer in `RingerRunner._log_attempt` still hard-codes the literal. Today it does:
    notes_parts.append("raw_check_output_first_2000_chars:")
    notes_parts.append(verify.raw_output_excerpt)
and the parts are later joined with "\n". Replace those two lines with exactly this one line, so the resulting notes text stays byte-identical:
    notes_parts.append(JEV_CHECK_OUTPUT_MARKER + verify.raw_output_excerpt)
After the change, the substring `raw_check_output_first_2000_chars` must appear exactly once in ringer.py (the constant's definition).

CHANGE 2 - delete the two dead FAIL-flag hooks
- Delete the `fail_flag_active` property from the `JevConfig` dataclass (keep `task_type_active` and the `fail_flag` field).
- Delete the line `self.jev_fail_flag_session = JevSession(config.jev, "fail_flag", self.jev_limiter)` from `RingerRunner.__init__` (keep `jev_task_type_session`).
- In tests/test_jev_plumbing.py, remove every assertion that references `fail_flag_active` (in the defaults test and in `test_a_feature_needs_the_master_switch_and_its_own`); keep the `task_type_active` assertions and keep the `config.fail_flag` default assertion.
- After the change, neither `fail_flag_active` nor `jev_fail_flag_session` appears anywhere in ringer.py or tests/.

CHANGE 3 - the task_type cache loader must not admit entries that later crash lint and run
Bug, reproduced end to end: `load_jev_cache` in ringer.py skips unparseable lines, but a line that is valid JSON with the right `key`, `contract`, and a dict `answer` is admitted even when it lacks `model` or `usage`, or its answer's `confidence` is not a number. `jev_task_type_fields` and `jev_task_type_lint_line` then index `entry["model"]` / `entry["usage"]` and format `confidence` with `:.2f`, and `decide_task_type` calls `float(confidence)`, so `./ringer.py lint` and `run` die with rc 2 (`error: 'model'`, `could not convert string to float: 'high'`).
Fix it in `load_jev_cache` only (every consumer routes through it): in the existing skip condition, also skip an entry when any of these holds:
- `entry.get("model")` is not a str
- `entry.get("usage")` is not a dict
- `answer.get("choice")` is not a str
- `answer.get("confidence")` is not a real number - use the existing helper `_jev_number(value)` (bool is not a number)
- `answer.get("probabilities")` is not a dict
Entries written by `jev_task_type_store` always satisfy these, so valid caches are unaffected. Keep the "never raises" docstring promise.
Add one test method to tests/test_jev_task_type.py, next to the existing test that calls `ringer.load_jev_cache` (it builds entries with a local `entry(choice)` helper): write a cache file holding one good entry plus one valid-JSON line for each of the five bad shapes above (each with a distinct key, all with contract "task_type-v1"), and assert only the good entry's key is loaded.

HOW TO RUN
- Targeted: `python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_jev_plumbing.py tests/test_jev_task_type.py tests/test_triage.py`
- Full: `python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`

WHAT THE CHECK VERIFIES
- `raw_check_output_first_2000_chars` occurs exactly once in ringer.py, and the line `notes_parts.append(JEV_CHECK_OUTPUT_MARKER + verify.raw_output_excerpt)` is present.
- `fail_flag_active` and `jev_fail_flag_session` occur nowhere in ringer.py or tests/.
- The check writes its own cache file with each of the five bad shapes plus a good entry and asserts `load_jev_cache` returns only the good one.
- End to end: with `[jev] enabled = true, task_type = true` pointed at a closed loopback port and a cache file holding a matching entry that lacks `model`, and separately one whose confidence is the string "high", `./ringer.py lint` exits 0 (today it exits 2).
- The full test suite passes both with RINGER_NO_CATALOG_REFRESH unset and with it set to 1, with pytest's PytestReturnNotNoneWarning treated as an error. Run `python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` yourself before finishing (about 70 seconds).
- `git add -A` stages only paths in the ownership list, every owned path is changed, and no added line contains the em dash.

import ast, re, sys
rep = open("tests/test_jev_fail_replay.py", encoding="utf-8").read()
stub = open("tests/jev_stub.py", encoding="utf-8").read()
errs = []
if "os.environ.copy()" in rep: errs.append("tests/test_jev_fail_replay.py still builds env with os.environ.copy()")
if re.search(r"^PROXY_VARS\s*=", rep, re.M): errs.append("tests/test_jev_fail_replay.py still defines PROXY_VARS")
if "jev_cli_env(" not in rep: errs.append("tests/test_jev_fail_replay.py does not call jev_cli_env")
tree = ast.parse(stub)
cls = next((n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "JevCliTestCase"), None)
cli = next((n for n in cls.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "cli"), None) if cls else None
if not cli: errs.append("JevCliTestCase.cli not found")
else:
    body = ast.get_source_segment(stub, cli)
    if "jev_cli_env(" not in body: errs.append("JevCliTestCase.cli does not call jev_cli_env")
    if "os.environ.copy()" in body: errs.append("JevCliTestCase.cli still builds env with os.environ.copy()")
if not any(isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "jev_cli_env" for n in tree.body): errs.append("module-level jev_cli_env not defined in tests/jev_stub.py")
print("\n".join(errs)); sys.exit(1 if errs else 0)
